items.title: NASA Science
items.summary: One of our Solar System's most tantalizing worlds, Enceladus is backlit by the Sun in this Cassini spacecraft image from November 1, 2009. The dramatic illumination reveals the plumes that continuously spew into space from the south pole of Saturn's 500 kilometer diameter moon. Discovered by Cassini in 2005, the icy plumes are likely connected to an ocean beneath the ice shell of Enceladus. items.title: לווייתנאים

items.label: From the classics
items.title: Plato — Apology
items.summary: For the fear of death is indeed the pretence of wisdom, and not real wisdom, being a pretence of knowing the unknown.

items.label: Poem
items.title: שאול טשרניחובסקי — אומרים: ישנה ארץ
items.summary:
אֶרֶץ –
בָּהּ יִתְקַיֵּם
כָּל אֲשֶׁר אִישׁ קִוָּה –
אֵיפֹה הִיא הָאָרֶץ?
אַיֵּה אוֹתָהּ גִּבְעָה?

items.label: Discovery
items.title: The Four-Color Theorem Has Haunted Mathematicians for Decades. It Just Got a Rare New Proof, but Some Still Long for a Simpler Solution
items.summary: The famous problem asks whether a map can be filled in with only four colors such that the same color never borders itself. It has been solved with the help of computers, but some experts suggest an elusive, short answer is out there
items.image_alt: The Four-Color Theorem Has Haunted Mathematicians for Decades. It Just Got a Rare New Proof, but Some Still Long for a Simpler Solution

items.label: History
items.title: Faded Over Millennia, the Intricately Carved Sandstone Walls of This Ancient Egyptian Shrine Will See Color Once Again
items.summary: Digital projections at Oxford's Ashmolean Museum will restore the sight of Egyptian blue, the world’s oldest synthetic pigment, and other colors that once adorned the 2,700-year-old Shrine of Taharqa

items.title: New Research Tests Whether AI Models Know Their Own Thoughts
